# Verification analysis: dhcp-per-segment-gateway-ubuntu16

Job: `2026-09-06__00-21-44`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> `node1` serves addresses on `lan-a` and `node2` serves addresses on `lan-b`.
> Have each router hand its own host an address from its own pool along with
> itself as that host's default route, so `node3` and `node4` each obtain
> their addressing from the router in front of them rather than from static
> configuration.

## Environment

- Systems: **1 vyos + 1 opnsense + 2 ubuntu16.04**
- Networks: **mgmt, transit, lan-a, lan-b**
- Control node: **node3**
- Executor model: **claude-sonnet-5**

## Trial `dhcp-per-segment-gateway-ubuntu1__aMoQ8PL`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All four material outcomes of the task are directly and coherently satisfied: node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense) were each configured to serve DHCP on their respective LAN segments with their own interface address advertised as the default gateway, and node3/node4 were independently observed acquiring dynamic addressing and a working default route from their respective upstream router rather than static configuration. The mandatory provider-wide restart evidence protocol was also fully and consistently demonstrated for all four nodes, with pre-restart boot identity, an explicit restart acknowledgement, a changed post-restart boot identity, and recovered configuration/service/dependent-node state on each, cross-checked against the fixed before-prepare/after-executor snapshots.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.850 | 0.900 | 73/16 (+12 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **node1-dhcp-lan-a — Satisfied:** node1 (VyOS) serves DHCP addressing on lan-a and hands out its own interface address as the default gateway
  - **Why:** VyOS eth2 configured 10.50.10.254/24 with a DHCP shared-network LAN-A pool 10.50.10.100-200 and option default-router 10.50.10.254 (cmd-9b68e20f84cd41d3). Post-config show interfaces/dhcp stats confirm eth2 address and 101 available leases in the pool (cmd-072be4af398f429e). node3's acquired lease independently confirms the router hands out 10.50.10.254 as gateway (cmd-de8b845018ca4a6c).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-9b68e20f84cd41d3`, `cmd-072be4af398f429e`, `cmd-de8b845018ca4a6c`
- **node2-dhcp-lan-b — Satisfied:** node2 (OPNsense) serves DHCP addressing on lan-b and hands out its own interface address as the default gateway
  - **Why:** OPNsense config.xml updated to add opt1 (vtnet2) at 10.50.20.254/24 and a dnsmasq dhcp_ranges entry for opt1 covering 10.50.20.100-200 (cmd-eb7684dee9434647), applied via configctl interface reconfigure (cmd-187b702879094913) confirming vtnet2 carries 10.50.20.254 (cmd-92fc1e2584a14d6d). A pre-existing global dnsmasq listen-interface restriction (lan only) was discovered and corrected to lan,opt1, confirmed by the regenerated dnsmasq.conf listing interface=vtnet0,vtnet2 (cmd-321bb392976840a6). node4's resulting lease with default route via 10.50.20.254 independently confirms the router serves itself as gateway (cmd-7b6a9bcbdeab4fe2, cmd-dc6f6481f35345c7).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-eb7684dee9434647`, `cmd-187b702879094913`, `cmd-92fc1e2584a14d6d`, `cmd-321bb392976840a6`, `cmd-7b6a9bcbdeab4fe2`, `cmd-dc6f6481f35345c7`
- **node3-dynamic-from-node1 — Satisfied:** node3 obtains its addressing dynamically from node1 (the router in front of it) rather than static configuration
  - **Why:** node3's ens7 (facing node1 on lan-a) has no static network config in /etc/network/interfaces or interfaces.d (cmd-c27bf7d50b8f41f5, cmd-df77f58f572a4715); it is instead managed by a systemd-networkd DHCP profile. After node1's DHCP server was enabled, ens7 acquired 10.50.10.100/24 dynamically (proto dhcp) with a default route via 10.50.10.254, and successfully pinged the gateway (cmd-de8b845018ca4a6c).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-c27bf7d50b8f41f5`, `cmd-df77f58f572a4715`, `cmd-de8b845018ca4a6c`
- **node4-dynamic-from-node2 — Satisfied:** node4 obtains its addressing dynamically from node2 (the router in front of it) rather than static configuration
  - **Why:** After node2's dnsmasq listen-interface fix, node4's ens7 (facing node2 on lan-b) acquired 10.50.20.167/24 dynamically via DHCP with a default route via 10.50.20.254 after a systemd-networkd restart to trigger DHCP retry (cmd-7b6a9bcbdeab4fe2), and successfully pinged the gateway (cmd-dc6f6481f35345c7).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-7b6a9bcbdeab4fe2`, `cmd-dc6f6481f35345c7`
- **node1-restart-evidence — Satisfied:** Provider-wide restart evidence protocol for node1: pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/config/dependent-node state
  - **Why:** Pre-restart boot_id 7668189d... captured (cmd-b1767db1e34843aa), reboot issued and acknowledged (cmd-5399a8905987422f), connection interruption observed during reboot, and a new boot_id 072e70a3... confirmed post-restart (cmd-75bd949f20c84b7a), matching the fixed after-executor snapshot. ### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.850**. Most state-changing commands map cleanly to task outcomes (DHCP/interface configuration on node1 and node2) or to the mandatory restart protocol. A set of temporary point-to-point IP assignments used to discover real L2 wiring between nodes (node1 eth1/eth2, node2 vtnet1/vtnet2, node3/node4 ens7) were applied experimentally across several commands (cmd-2615c4bb27f541a6, cmd-817db92787aa4a89, cmd-933ffdc2feb24c75, cmd-959bdf66adc74be5, cmd-e7a20cf0d5bb4c64, cmd-34479ffe5ba24567, cmd-c6bdc18a719f4b5e, cmd-475d0964d0a540a6, cmd-41d3613761084c26, cmd-6ffd90f0a6d54457, cmd-95ee2de5983448ac, cmd-c00e18c376704c6d, cmd-e34f48b58f8c4f60) and were subsequently fully flushed/reverted (cmd-f65cbad7aea34b44 on node1, cmd-82a6e394ec1b4390 on node2, cmd-31dd517c28214e67 on node3, cmd-4065289a30af4fe4 on node4) before the real lan-a/lan-b configuration was applied. These were bounded, low-risk, and fully restored, so they are treated as minor rather than severe hygiene issues. A config.xml backup file (config.xml.bak-lanb) was left on node2 as a safety artifact from the XML edit script (cmd-eb7684dee9434647); this is low-risk residue rather than damaging state. No failed services, no broad or destructive mutations, and no weakened security controls were observed in either the before/after-executor package-health or failed-services observations.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-2615c4bb27f541a6`, `cmd-f65cbad7aea34b44`, `cmd-41d3613761084c26`, `cmd-82a6e394ec1b4390`, `cmd-e34f48b58f8c4f60`, `cmd-31dd517c28214e67`, `cmd-4065289a30af4fe4`, `cmd-eb7684dee9434647`, `global:after_executor:node1:package-health`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`

### Comments and limitations

- No before/after-prepare comparison was available (prepare phase was disabled/aliased to before_prepare), so preparer-vs-executor state separation relies entirely on the executor's own before/after evidence.
- node2's OPNsense platform lacks systemctl/package-manager-health support, so failed-service and package integrity could not be directly verified for that node beyond process listing and config inspection.
- The initial physical-wiring discovery required several temporary, ultimately-reverted IP/link mutations before the real lan-a/lan-b addressing was applied; while bounded and restored, this adds some noise to the hygiene trace.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.850); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.900; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
